## Lattices

### `query.contract`

Ordinary queries return PostgreSQL's rows. An index changes how a query runs, never what it returns. Both servers sort text in C order, so collation plays no part.

| Member | `server.doltgres` | `server.postgres` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index_never_changes_results` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `not_exists_over_nullable_foreign_key` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `exists_over_nullable_indexed_columns` | ❌ | ✅ |

### `txn.contract`

What PostgreSQL guarantees to concurrent transactions. A write that reports success is never lost. A server may refuse a write with an error such as 40001, but it must not report success and then drop it.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `concurrent_updates_lose_nothing_autocommit` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `concurrent_updates_lose_nothing_in_transactions` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `concurrent_upserts_lose_nothing` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `concurrent_transfers_keep_the_total` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `unique_key_holds_under_concurrent_inserts` | ✅ | ✅ |
